code taken from tutorial 4 learning from biostats

##parametric route

reading in the data
```{r}
pills <- read.csv(file.choose(), header = TRUE)
```

installing/loading in packages
```{r}
install.packages("pgirmess")
library(stats)
library(pgirmess)
library(psych)
```

aov is the anova test and the results are attached to the time.fit and summary allows us to seethe results
```{r}
time.fit <- aov(Time ~ as.factor(Exposure_Level), data = pills)
```

before analysing the output we need to test the data for noramlity and homogeny of variances
here were testing the normality of the residuals and making two graphs to see them
```{r}
time.res <- resid(time.fit)
qqnorm(time.res)
qqline(time.res)
hist(time.res)
```

shaprio-wilks test for the normal distribution
p>0.05 normal
p<0.05 not normal
```{r}
shapiro.test(time.res)
```

testing for the homogeneity of variance with Bartlett test
p>0.05 homogeneous
p<0.05 not homogeneous
```{r}
bartlett.test(Time ~ Exposure_Level, pills)
```

flingers test
p>0.05 homogeneous
p<0.05 not homogeneous
```{r}
library(e1071)
fligner.test(Time ~ Exposure_Level, pills)
```

boxplot of pills data
```{r}
boxplot(Time ~ Exposure_Level, 
        data = pills, 
        ylab = "Time (s)", 
        xlab = "Exposure Level", 
        main = "Effect of maze completion time on amount of exposures",
        las = 1)
box()
```

look at the summary
```{r}
summary(time.fit)
```

we want to further investigate the impact of exposures on the specific groups so we will
use a post-Hoc test called Tukey from the stats package
this is done if the ANOVA is found to be significant to determine which groups vary from which, a multiple comparisons test of the treatment groups
p adj >0.05 not significant different groups
p adj <0.05 significant different groups
```{r}
TukeyHSD(time.fit)
```

##data transforming

transforming code!
the square brackets is telling R which [row, column] to go to in this case we want to look 
at the enirety of the second column (which is the Time variable of our pills data)
now that the pills2 data has been transformed the ANOVA test will be run in the same chunk
this is an example of the log10 transforming
```{r}
pills2 <- pills
pills2[, 2] <- log10(pills2[, 2])
time.fit2 <- aov(Time ~ as.factor(Exposure_Level), pills2)
time.res2 <- resid(time.fit2)
```

re-test parametric assumption
remember
p>0.05 normal/homogeneous
p<0.05 not normal/not homogeneous
```{r}
shapiro.test(time.res2)
bartlett.test(Time ~ Exposure_Level, pills2)
```

boxplot of new pills data
```{r}
boxplot(Time ~ Exposure_Level, 
        data = pills2, 
        ylab = "Time (s)", 
        xlab = "Exposure Level", 
        main = "Effect of maze completion time on amount of exposures",
        las = 1)
box()
```

look at the new summary
```{r}
summary(time.fit2)
```


##non parametric route

non parametric!
this is for when transforming the data didnt work earlier
since its non-parametric we dont have to test any assumptions since there isnt any
the non parametric equivalent is the Kruskal-Wallis test
```{r}
kruskal.test(Time ~ as.factor(Exposure_Level), data = pills)
```

now for the non-parametric post-hoc equivalent
```{r}
kruskalmc(Time ~ as.factor(Exposure_Level), data = pills)
```
